newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan gets rousing reception from party.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan gets rousing reception from party.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan got a rousing reception from his Islamist party at a congress on Sunday that followed his worst week in power.

More than 10,000 Welfare Party supporters, waving flags and hand-held "sparkler" fireworks, cheered as Erbakan entered a sports hall to the accompanyment of marches played by a traditional Ottoman band.
"In the name of Allah, the merciful, the forgiver," Erbakan said in Turkish, quoting the opening lines of the Koran, at the start of a speech.
Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist leader, has been battered by a disastrous trip to Libya that exposed Turkey to criticism from both his hosts and Ankara's NATO ally Washington.
He faces an opposition challenge to his three-month-old rule on Wednesday over the trip but he is expected to survive any censure motion against him.
His coalition with the pro-Western True Path Party (DYP) of Tansu Ciller has five more MPs than the 276 neeeded to guarantee toppling the government.
